I’ve just finished a large batch of file edits: added enemy.js, remote.js, updated world.js with performance tweaks and multiplayer spawn points, rewrote index.html to include lobby UI, and overhauled main.js to wire together netcode, bots, and the new HUD. All those changes are now saved in the repository under D:\fps. The user’s last request was “Now build, then run an automated server test simulating two clients through the lobby flow.” 

First I need to confirm what “build” means in this project. Looking at the existing package.json (which I recall from earlier steps contains a Vite build script), the standard way to compile the TypeScript/JS sources into a production bundle is `npm run build`. The user wants to see the build output, but only the tail end to verify it succeeded, so piping through `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` in PowerShell will capture both stdout and stderr and then show the last five lines, which should include any errors or the final “built in X ms” message.

I considered using a plain `npm run build` without redirection, but that would dump the entire log to the chat, which could be overwhelming. Using the PowerShell command with `Select-Object -Last 5` is concise and matches the pattern I've used earlier for quick diagnostics. I also thought about running a separate test script after the build, but the user explicitly said “Now build, then run an automated server test…”. The immediate next step is to trigger the build; once I have the build result I can decide how to invoke the server test (likely via a node script or a test runner). But the user asked for both actions in one go. However, I don’t have a ready-made test command; the safest incremental approach is to first ensure the build succeeds. If the build fails, the subsequent test would be meaningless. So I will issue a tool call to PowerShell to run `npm run build` with the tail‑filter, labeling the description as “Build the game with vite”. This satisfies the user’s immediate request to build and gives a concise output for verification.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is a PowerShell execution of `npm run build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` with a clear description. This will give me the build status and allow me to proceed to the automated server test in the next step.
